title: Rethinking Privileged Information in On-Policy Self-Distillation
abstract: arXiv:2608.18271v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) trains a student on its own responses using token-level supervision from the same model conditioned on privileged reference information. We investigate whether performance gains from OPSD show that the student learned the information in the reference or instead reflect recovery of reasoning behavior already present in the base model. We perform OPSD experiments on science and mathematics datasets using Qwen3 models ranging from 1.7B to 8B. Our analysis framework separates the supervision induced by the reference from the supervision provided by the teacher without the reference and measures how each aligns with changes in the student's predictions. The correct reference does not provide a consistent performance benefit across teacher generation modes, model sizes, and training datasets. Students can improve without the correct reference, and a solution from another problem can outperform the correct sol

translated_title: 重新思考在线策略自蒸馏中的特权信息
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.18271v1 公告类型：新 摘要：在线策略自蒸馏（OPSD）通过使用来自同一模型的、以特权参考信息为条件的令牌级监督，训练学生模型基于其自身响应进行学习。我们研究了OPSD带来的性能提升是否表明学生学习了参考中的信息，还是仅仅反映了基础模型中已存在的推理行为的恢复。我们使用Qwen3模型（参数范围从1.7B到8B）在科学和数学数据集上进行了OPSD实验。我们的分析框架将参考信息引起的监督与无参考的教师提供的监督分开，并测量每种监督与学生预测变化的一致性。正确的参考在教师生成模式、模型大小和训练数据集之间并未提供一致的性能优势。学生可以在没有正确参考的情况下改进，而来自其他问题的解决方案有时能胜过正确的解决方案。
tldr: 本研究发现，在线策略自蒸馏中的特权参考信息并非持续带来性能提升，学生的改进可能源于基础模型中已有的推理能力，而非真正学习参考信息。
en_tdlr: This study finds that privileged reference information in on-policy self-distillation does not consistently improve performance, and student gains may reflect existing reasoning abilities in the base model rather than learning from the reference.
